items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Later on we got to be good friends.

ctx.x: That‟s what I said: the Red Norvo in February of ‟54. Then Woody Herman in March of ‟54 with Panama Francis on the gig. He‟s playing on Mess Around, which I presume was – did Ertegun write that for Ray Charles? Anyway, that‟s Woody Herman, a Woody Herman date. There are several between them. I‟m showing in late ‟53, Four Freshmen, then Dick Lewis. Any of these ringing a bell?
Dick was the British Stan Kenton. He had a band too. Stan gave him a lot of charts. So he‟d recorded some of my things. Later on we got to be good friends. The Four Freshmen I don‟t know about.

We‟ll go back up, look at that one. That was Four Freshman. Actually, they‟re not showing – did you? – I‟m wondering if you would contribute, if they did an arrangement of yours. But they‟re not showing any credits for any. It was with Stan, Stan‟s orchestra.
